concepts.def: Region where gravity is so strong even light cannot escape.
Boundary around a black hole; no return point.
Radius of the event horizon of a non-rotating black hole.
Tiny stellar remnant of mostly neutrons; supernova leftover.
Rotating neutron star emitting beams of radio waves.
Extremely bright active galactic nucleus powered by a black hole.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a massive star's core after supernova exceeds ~3 solar masses, even neutron pressure cannot stop collapse. Gravity wins and a black hole forms with an event horizon from which nothing escapes.
Most large galaxies host a supermassive black hole at their centre. The Milky Way's is Sagittarius A*, about 4 million solar masses. M87's is ~6.5 billion solar masses (first imaged 2019).
A spinning neutron star with a strong magnetic field sweeps radio beams across space. When the beam crosses Earth, we detect regular pulses — like a cosmic lighthouse.
